verdict.rationale: Obsidian's local-first design (plain Markdown files stored on device) gives users direct control over retention and deletion, and Obsidian Sync is end-to-end encrypted by default so not even the Obsidian team can access notes. However, there is no documentation on deleting data from Sync or Publish servers, no stated retention periods, and version history in Sync retains historical copies rather than supporting deletion, so server-side data lifecycle control is unclear. Missing for 10: explicit account/data-deletion policy for Sync and Publish servers, retention period documentation, independent confirmation that deleted local files are purged from cloud backups.
